rule_description: Agreements restraining a party from exercising a lawful profession, trade, or business are void, subject to statutory and judicial exceptions (e.g. sale-of-goodwill exception under the proviso to S.27).
trigger_condition: clausexplain_category == 'Non-Compete' AND restriction is not limited to a narrow, reasonable scope (duration/geography/activity)
risk_effect: restraint-of-trade concern (flag for review, not automatic voidness)
exception_condition: Narrowly drafted restraints tied to the sale of goodwill of a business are a recognized statutory exception; reasonableness is fact-specific and ultimately a judicial question.

rule_description: No-solicit clauses (customers or employees) may be assessed under the same restraint-of-trade doctrine as non-compete clauses, depending on scope.
trigger_condition: clausexplain_category == 'Non-Solicitation' AND restriction is broad/indefinite in scope or duration
exception_condition: Reasonable, narrowly-scoped protections of legitimate business interests are treated differently by courts than blanket restraints; this varies by case.

rule_description: Agreements that absolutely restrict a party's right to enforce contractual rights through ordinary legal proceedings are void.
trigger_condition: clausexplain_category == 'Dispute Resolution' AND clause text indicates an absolute bar on legal proceedings (not merely a mandatory arbitration/forum-selection clause)
exception_condition: Section 28 has a statutory exception for arbitration agreements; a clause that merely channels disputes to arbitration is NOT automatically caught by this section, and must not be flagged the same way as an absolute bar on court access.

rule_description: Where a contract names a sum payable on breach (whether termed 'penalty' or 'liquidated damages'), the aggrieved party is entitled to reasonable compensation not exceeding the amount named, regardless of the label used.
trigger_condition: clausexplain_category == 'Penalties' AND a specific monetary sum or formula is named as payable on breach
risk_effect: penalty/damages concern (the named sum is a ceiling, not an automatic entitlement)
exception_condition: Where the sum represents a genuine, reasonable pre-estimate proportionate to likely loss, courts are generally less likely to intervene; extremely disproportionate sums attract more scrutiny.

rule_description: In the absence of a specific liquidated-damages clause, a party suffering loss from breach is entitled to compensation for loss/damage naturally arising from the breach, or that the parties knew was likely to result from it.
trigger_condition: clausexplain_category == 'Liability' AND no cap or specific damages formula is present (i.e. Section 73's default rule would apply)
risk_effect: context only -- describes the statutory default that applies when the contract is silent, not itself a risk trigger
exception_condition: Remote or indirect losses not reasonably foreseeable at the time of contracting are generally excluded under the general rule of foreseeability.

rule_description: Where a party refuses to perform, or disables itself from performing, its promise in its entirety, the other party may treat the contract as rescinded, unless it has signaled acceptance of continued performance.
trigger_condition: clausexplain_category == 'Termination' AND clause addresses termination for breach/non-performance
risk_effect: context only -- describes background statutory right, relevant when assessing whether a termination-for-breach clause narrows or expands this default right
exception_condition: The non-breaching party's conduct after the breach (e.g. continuing to accept performance) can affect whether this right survives.

rule_description: A party that rightfully rescinds a contract is entitled to compensation for any damage sustained through the non-fulfilment of the contract.
trigger_condition: clausexplain_category == 'Termination' AND clause is silent on post-termination compensation for the terminating party
risk_effect: context only -- background statutory entitlement, not itself a defect in the clause

rule_description: The consideration or object of an agreement is unlawful, and the agreement is void, if it is forbidden by law, is of such a nature that it would defeat the provisions of any law, is fraudulent, involves injury to person/property, or is regarded by the court as immoral or opposed to public policy.
trigger_condition: clause text suggests the underlying subject matter or purpose of the obligation may itself be unlawful (rare in ordinary commercial contracts)
risk_effect: context only -- a general validity backstop, expected to trigger rarely in ordinary commercial/service contracts

legal_provision: Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development (MSMED) Act, 2006, Section 15
rule_description: A buyer must make payment to a micro or small enterprise supplier on or before the date agreed in writing, or, where no date is agreed, within 15 days of acceptance of goods/services; in no case can the agreed period exceed 45 days from the day of acceptance.
trigger_condition: clausexplain_category == 'Payment' AND supplier is a registered micro or small enterprise under the MSMED Act AND agreed/implied payment period exceeds 45 days
risk_effect: potentially non-compliant concern -- statutory ceiling on credit period
exception_condition: This protection applies ONLY where the supplier is registered as a micro or small enterprise under the Udyam registration framework. It does NOT automatically apply to every freelancer or every SME -- registration status must be separately verified and must not be assumed from context alone. Medium enterprises are not covered by this specific delayed-payment protection.

rule_description: Where a buyer fails to pay a registered micro/small enterprise supplier within the Section 15 period, the buyer is liable to pay compound interest with monthly rests, at three times the bank rate notified by the Reserve Bank of India, from the appointed date.
trigger_condition: clausexplain_category == 'Payment' AND supplier is a registered micro/small enterprise AND clause disclaims or is silent on late-payment interest
risk_effect: potentially non-compliant concern -- statutory interest entitlement cannot be contracted away for a covered supplier
exception_condition: Applies only where the Section 15 registration condition above is met; contractual clauses purporting to waive this right for a covered MSME supplier are the specific concern this rule targets.

legal_provision: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, Section 6 (consent)
rule_description: Processing of personal data generally requires free, specific, informed, unconditional, and unambiguous consent from the data principal, given through clear affirmative action, for a specified purpose.
trigger_condition: clausexplain_category == 'Privacy / Data Protection' AND clause authorizes processing of personal data without describing a consent mechanism
exception_condition: Certain 'legitimate uses' under the DPDPA (e.g. specified employment purposes, compliance with law) do not require separate consent -- verify against the current statutory text and rules before treating absence of a consent clause as automatically deficient.

legal_provision: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, Section 8 (obligations of Data Fiduciary)
rule_description: A Data Fiduciary must implement reasonable security safeguards to prevent personal data breaches and must notify the Data Protection Board and affected data principals in the event of a breach.
trigger_condition: clausexplain_category == 'Privacy / Data Protection' AND clause is silent on security safeguards or breach notification
source: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (bare act) -- VERIFY current rules/notifications before publication

legal_provision: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, Section 8 (data retention)
rule_description: A Data Fiduciary must erase personal data, and ensure any Data Processor engaged by it erases the data, when the specified purpose is no longer being served and retention is not required for legal compliance.
trigger_condition: clausexplain_category == 'Privacy / Data Protection' AND clause does not specify a data retention or deletion schedule
exception_condition: Legal retention requirements under other applicable laws can justify continued retention beyond the immediate purpose.
source: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (bare act) -- VERIFY current rules/notifications before publication

rule_description: Section 124 defines a contract of indemnity (a promise to save the other party from loss caused by the promisor or a third person); Section 125 sets out the indemnity-holder's rights when sued in respect of the indemnified matter. Indian law does not impose a general statutory cap on indemnity amounts the way Section 74 caps named sums on breach.
trigger_condition: clausexplain_category == 'Indemnification' AND indemnity obligation is uncapped or unusually broad in scope
risk_effect: excessive liability concern (a commercial-fairness flag, not itself a statutory violation, since Indian law does not cap indemnity the way it caps penalties)

legal_provision: Indian Contract Act, 1872, Section 56 (doctrine of frustration)
rule_description: A contract to do an act that becomes impossible, or unlawful, after the contract is made, becomes void. This is a background common-law-adjacent statutory doctrine that fills the gap when a contract has NO express force majeure clause -- it does not describe how to interpret an existing clause.
trigger_condition: clausexplain_category == 'Force Majeure' AND the contract contains no force majeure clause at all (i.e. this rule flags an ABSENCE, detected at the contract level, not a property of a specific span)
risk_effect: context only -- flags reliance on a strict, narrowly-applied default doctrine in place of a negotiated clause
exception_condition: Section 56 is applied narrowly by Indian courts (mere hardship or commercial impracticability is generally insufficient); this is a coarse gap-filling flag, not a substitute for an actual force-majeure risk assessment.
